_README: Machine-readable BLOCKED-RUST-EFFECT residue worklist. Built by the round-54 full programmatic residue re-walk (Agent N3); round-55 (Agent N1) hardened the cron that reads it from a purely-lexical resolver to a structural one. The per-entry staleness arms of scripts/check_audit_coverage_staleness.py read THIS file (not the prose audit). LEXICAL arm (round-54): FAILs if any `genuinely_missing` entry's `claimed_missing_effect` (resolved through `aliases`) actually exists as a live Rust Effect:: variant AND a wired _ta_dict_to_python_effect bridge arm. STRUCTURAL arm (round-55, additive, never-blocking — same post-commit-hook contract: the hook ignores the exit code): (a) every `genuinely_missing` entry MUST carry a SHA-shaped `verified_absent_at_commit` (the commit at which a human/agent actually re-verified genuine absence via live-enum + bridge + name-in-wired-arm) — a missing/garbled stamp is `residue_unverified`; (b) the stamp goes stale and yields `residue_needs_reverify` if ANY commit after it touched rust/src/cards.rs or src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py (the only two files whose changes can ship/bridge an Effect — the exact Pulsar mechanism; git-history absence soft-skips and never false-flags); (c) NON-LEXICAL Pulsar catch: if the card's printed name appears in a LIVE, wired bridge-arm block whose kind resolves to a live Rust Effect:: variant, it is `residue_stale` (hard, NOT ack-suppressible) when that arm's kind also matches a curated alias, else `residue_suspect_needs_reverify` (never-blocking) — suppressible ONLY by an audited per-arm `name_in_arm_ack` (a hand-re-walked 'this wired arm is a DIFFERENT ability of the same card, claimed effect genuinely absent' acknowledgment; per-arm, so a second un-acked arm or a renamed acked arm still surfaces). This closes the gap that let Pulsar Squadron Ace (Effect LookAtTopNRevealOrCounter shipped r28/29, plan-name ChoiceTriggerSpacecraftRevealOrCounter never lexically resolved) pass the r54 re-walk + cron silently. `closed` entries are the historical reclassifications kept for the cron's lexical regression check (they MUST resolve to a live+bridged variant; if one stops resolving, the closure prose itself went stale) and do NOT carry the round-55 fields. To close a residue card: flip its `status` to `closed`, set `resolved_variant`, drop `verified_absent_at_commit`/`name_in_arm_ack`, and sync EOE_PROBE_READINESS_AUDIT.md. See scripts/check_audit_coverage_staleness.py docstring.

_schema.entry: short stable label (matches the audit per-card row)
_schema.claimed_missing_effect: the plan-invented / audit-named Effect the residue row asserts is missing
_schema.aliases: candidate real Rust Effect:: variant names the claimed name could actually be (plan-name -> real-variant resolution; first one present in the live enum wins)
_schema.status: genuinely_missing = audit correctly lists it as BLOCKED-RUST-EFFECT (cron asserts it stays missing); closed = effect arm shipped + bridged, reclassified out (cron asserts it stays resolvable)
_schema.verified_absent_at_commit: REQUIRED on every `genuinely_missing` entry (round-55). A SHA-shaped (7-40 hex) git commit at which a human/agent actually re-verified the claimed effect is genuinely absent: no alias resolves to a live Rust Effect:: variant, the printed name is not in any wired bridge-arm that ships a live Effect (or any such arm is name_in_arm_ack-ed as a different ability), and there is no wired bridge arm. CADENCE: refresh the stamp once ANY commit after it has touched rust/src/cards.rs or src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py — the only two files that can ship/bridge an Effect. The cron emits `residue_unverified` (missing/garbled) or `residue_needs_reverify` (stale by cadence); both never-blocking. Omitted on `closed` entries.
_schema.name_in_arm_ack: OPTIONAL on a `genuinely_missing` entry (round-55). A bridge-arm `kind` string (or list of strings) the human re-walked and confirmed is a DIFFERENT ability of the same card — so the card's printed name legitimately appears in that wired arm while the CLAIMED effect is still genuinely absent (e.g. Command Bridge's mana ability in `add_mana_to_pool`; Meltstrider's Resolve's bare-bilateral Fight sibling in `fight_target_creature_with_target_creature`). Suppresses ONLY the `residue_suspect_needs_reverify` row for that EXACT arm kind; never suppresses a hard alias-matched `residue_stale` row, and a second un-acked arm (or a renamed acked arm) still surfaces.
_schema.resolved_variant: for closed entries: the live Rust Effect:: variant the effect actually shipped as
_schema.reclassified_to: for closed entries: the residual non-Effect blocker bucket
